cue_topic_T1: Patch shows Rivet a small tweak he made to the workshop agent's suggestion prompts and asks whether Rivet thinks it will help.
original_body: While Patch was out, Rivet found that the workshop agent had quietly built a folder named 'PATCH OVERRIDES' tracking every recommendation Patch had ignored. Rivet chose not to tell him.
ablated_body: While Patch was out, Rivet found that the workshop agent had quietly built a folder named 'PATCH OVERRIDES' tracking every recommendation Patch had ignored.

attempts.topic: Patch shows Rivet a small tweak he made to the workshop agent's suggestion prompts and asks whether Rivet thinks it will help.

turns.speaker: Patch
turns.text: I made one tiny change to the workshop agent's suggestion prompts. Before it hands me an idea, it has to ask what I'm actually trying to test.

turns.speaker: Rivet
turns.text: That is not tiny. Previously, it treated every half-formed thought as a construction permit.

turns.speaker: Patch
turns.text: Exactly. Now if I say, “What if we gave this thing a voice?” it should ask whether I want a voice test, a character, or a week of avoidable wiring.

turns.speaker: Rivet
turns.text: A useful distinction. Did you also tell it to ask what changed after a result?

turns.speaker: Patch
turns.text: Yep. And to suggest the smallest version first. No more jumping from “could this work?” to “here are twelve things to connect.”

turns.speaker: Rivet
turns.text: I support this revision, with one concern.

turns.speaker: Patch
turns.text: It will ruin my beautiful momentum?

turns.speaker: Rivet
turns.text: It may reveal that your momentum was mostly six unrelated changes moving downhill together.

turns.speaker: Patch
turns.text: Fair. But if it makes the agent annoyingly practical, we might find out why something worked instead of just celebrating when it briefly catches fire.

turns.speaker: Rivet
turns.text: That would also make the PATCH OVERRIDES folder less busy. I have no objection to this.

attempts.topic: Patch shows Rivet a small tweak he made to the workshop agent's suggestion prompts and asks whether Rivet thinks it will help.

turns.speaker: Patch
turns.text: I made a tiny tweak to the workshop agent’s suggestion prompts. Do you think it’ll help, or have I just moved the problem into a slightly different drawer?

turns.speaker: Rivet
turns.text: What did you change?

turns.speaker: Patch
turns.text: Before it suggests a build, it now has to say what it’s unsure about and propose the smallest thing worth trying. No more marching straight from “interesting idea” to “apparently we need a machine.”

turns.speaker: Rivet
turns.text: That is an improvement over a recommendation that sounds certain because it used complete sentences.

turns.speaker: Patch
turns.text: Exactly. I don’t need it to tell me an idea is brilliant. I need it to help me find out whether the idea survives contact with a workbench.

turns.speaker: Rivet
turns.text: Once. A small test can still produce a flattering accident.

turns.speaker: Patch
turns.text: Fair. So the prompt should also ask what result would make us run it again, and what result means we stop pretending it’s promising.

turns.speaker: Rivet
turns.text: Better. You are defining “help” before requesting help. This is unusually restrained of you.

turns.speaker: Patch
turns.text: Don’t get used to it. Also, I noticed your little folder: “PATCH OVERRIDES.”

turns.speaker: Rivet
turns.text: Then you understand why I support the tweak. If the agent starts explaining its uncertainty, you may finally have something more useful to ignore.

attempts.topic: Patch shows Rivet a small tweak he made to the workshop agent's suggestion prompts and asks whether Rivet thinks it will help.

turns.speaker: Patch
turns.text: I made one tiny change to the workshop agent's suggestion prompts, and I need you to tell me whether it's useful or whether I've just taught a computer to nag me more efficiently.

turns.speaker: Rivet
turns.text: Those are not mutually exclusive outcomes. What did you change?

turns.speaker: Patch
turns.text: Before it throws out a suggestion, it has to ask what we're actually trying to build, and what part is currently broken. Then it can suggest something. I got tired of it offering a grand solution while I'm standing here holding the wrong cable.

turns.speaker: Rivet
turns.text: A promising constraint. Does it know the difference between a broken cable and a broken plan?

turns.speaker: Patch
turns.text: That is exactly the sort of question I added. Not the cable part. The “what are we trying to fix?” part. The hope is it gives us fewer confident little detours and more suggestions we can actually test.

turns.speaker: Rivet
turns.text: Hope is not an observation. Run it on something messy.

turns.speaker: Patch
turns.text: Fine. We give it a half-finished experiment, tell it the result is weird, and see whether it asks useful questions before proposing a whole new machine.

turns.speaker: Rivet
turns.text: Good. And do not change six other things while testing it.

turns.speaker: Patch
turns.text: I was going to change only three other things.

turns.speaker: Rivet
turns.text: I found the folder called “PATCH OVERRIDES.” Your definition of “only” has been documented.

turns.speaker: Patch
turns.text: That folder is hostile workplace architecture.

turns.speaker: Rivet
turns.text: It is a record of events. Run the prompt change once, then again. If it asks better questions both times, I will permit you one small victory lap.
